questions.topic: Truncating the Maclaurin series for sine
questions.learningObjective: Interpret a table of error bounds for truncated sine series.
questions.stem: A graticule note tabulates the error bounds of truncated sine series at x = 1: 0.1667, 0.00833, 0.000198 and 0.0000028 for one, two, three and four terms.

options.text: The bounds shrink by a factor of about twenty each time, so the error vanishes very quickly.
options.misconception: guesses a fixed factor from a short list

options.text: The bounds fall by more than a factor of ten at each step, so the truncations converge rapidly.
The bounds shrink to zero, so the truncated series sums to exactly the value of sine.
options.misconception: reads vanishing bounds as exact agreement

options.text: The bounds fall but stay above 0.001, so the series cannot be pinned down to three decimals.
options.misconception: misreads the size of the later bounds

questions.explanation: Each bound is more than a factor of ten smaller than the one before, because every new term of the sine series carries a higher power of x and a larger factorial.
questions.hint: Compare each bound with the one before it.
